title: Conchiglie with Sausage Ragu
subtitle: Shell pasta in a slow-cooked Italian sausage and tomato sauce
excerpt: Shell-shaped pasta catches the ragu in every ridge. Italian pork sausage broken into chunks and simmered in tomatoes makes a sauce that feels far more effort than it is.
sourceNotes: Weeknight Italian ragu using pork sausage; shell pasta catches the sauce well.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the ragu alone for up to two months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat before tossing with freshly cooked pasta.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Make a large batch of ragu and freeze half.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The ragu improves overnight. Make it ahead and reheat gently before serving.

content.text: Conchiglie with sausage ragu is a forgiving, hands-off sauce. Squeeze the sausage meat out of the casings so it breaks into rough pieces and browns in the pan. A 25-minute simmer is all it takes to turn those pieces into a proper ragu. Do not rush the browning step or the sauce will be pale and bland.

Warm the olive oil in a wide frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the sausage meat in rough pieces. Cook without stirring for 3 minutes until browned, then break it up further and cook for 2 more minutes.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and fennel seeds if using. Cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in the red wine if using. Let it bubble and reduce for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and passata.
Stir well and simmer over a low heat for 25 minutes until the sauce is thick and the sausage is tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook the conchiglie in a large pan of salted boiling water until 2 minutes short of the packet time. Reserve a mug of pasta water and drain.
Add the pasta to the ragu. Toss over a medium heat for 2 minutes, adding pasta water as needed. Serve with parmesan.

items.symptom: The sausage is grey and tasteless.
items.cause: It was not browned properly before the onion and liquid were added.
items.fix: Brown the sausage meat first without disturbing it; let it sit in the hot pan for at least 3 minutes before stirring.

items.cause: The simmer was too short or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for at least 25 minutes over a steady low heat; the sauce should be thick enough to coat a spoon.

items.symptom: The pasta has no sauce clinging to it.
items.cause: The shapes were too small or the pasta was not tossed in the ragu.
items.fix: Conchiglie catches sauce in the cups; make sure to toss the pasta in the pan with the ragu rather than pouring sauce over plated pasta.
